items.title: Anthropic files to go public, disclosing $16.3 billion in first-half revenue
items.tldr: Anthropic's S-1 shows revenue jumping 14-fold to $16.3 billion in the first half of 2026, a first operating profit in Q2, and an unusual governance structure that keeps control away from public shareholders.
items.byline: The Next Web, MIT Technology Review

items.title: Meta plans up to $95 billion in new stock to fund AI, with Nvidia investing $3 billion
items.tldr: Meta launched about $35 billion of stock offerings plus a planned $60 billion at-the-market program to pay for AI infrastructure, and Nvidia committed $3 billion while expanding a chip and Muse partnership.

items.title: Build, Don't Play: Self-Improving LLM Research Agents Develop a Hearthstone Battlegrounds AI That Rivals Top Players
items.tldr: LLM research agents built a faithful Hearthstone Battlegrounds simulator and an RL agent in 20 days; the agent outperformed the server's top-10 players' recent results, while frontier LLMs playing directly fell far short.
items.byline: Changlian Ma, Limin Wang · Nanjing University, Shanghai AI Laboratory

items.title: Eat Your Precision: Precision Objective Mitigates Reward Hacking in Rubric-based RL
items.tldr: Rubric rewards for open-ended RL only measure coverage, so models learn to pad; adding a precision term for necessary, factually correct sentences raises win rate over the base model from 10.6% to 68.0%.
items.byline: Hyun Ryu, Jong-Heon Kim, Yiqing Xie et al. · KAIST AI, Carnegie Mellon University

items.title: S3AC: Stabilized, Selective, and Scalable Actor-Critic for LLM Reasoning
items.tldr: A recipe for training a value critic on long chain-of-thought lets actor-critic RL beat a modern GRPO variant from 1.5B to 397B parameters and train stably with a single rollout per prompt.
items.byline: Shuo Shen, Guangran Cheng, Chengqi Lyu et al. · Shanghai AI Laboratory

items.title: Thinking-in-Bets at Test Time Reduces Sycophantic Revisions in LLM Agents
items.tldr: Having an agent privately record its claims, evidence and confidence before reading user feedback sharply cuts sycophantic reversals of correct work while still letting it fix real bugs, without any training.

items.title: RynnVLA-Latent: Scaling Robotic Manipulation Foundation Models with 3D-Grounded Latent Actions
items.tldr: Alibaba's RynnVLA-Latent pretrains a robot policy on 30,100 hours of human, robot and simulation video using 3D-grounded latent actions, then adapts it to real robots, matching or edging out leading policies.
items.byline: Haoyu Zhao, Xingyue Zhao, Zhian Su et al. · DAMO Academy (Alibaba Group), Hupan Lab, CUHK

items.title: Moonshot launches Kimi K3.1 Pro, a near-frontier model with open weights promised by Nov 4
items.tldr: Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 Pro scores within a few points of Claude Opus 5.5 on agentic coding and an independent index, costs half as much, and is due as open weights by Nov 4.

items.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6.1 Terra, a cheaper and faster computer-use model
items.tldr: OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Terra costs $1/$5 per million tokens and, by OpenAI's measurements, matches GPT-6 Astra on a professional-task benchmark at a tenth of the price; OpenAI rates it Critical for cybersecurity.

items.title: Rewriting Scaling Laws for Synthetic Data with Compute and Data Constraints
items.tldr: A scaling law that charges for the compute spent generating synthetic rewrites predicts how much of a pretraining corpus should be rewritten, and shows that models trained on rewrites can beat the rewriter.
items.byline: Nicholas Roberts, Ahmed Ahmed, Suhas Kotha et al. · Princeton University, Stanford University, Jane Street

items.title: On-Policy Self-Training: Data-Free Self-Improvement in Large Language Models
items.tldr: Given only topic names, a model writes its own problems and answer hints, then distills from a copy of itself that sees the hints, improving MMLU by 10 points with no curated prompts or answers.
items.byline: Leon Sick, Lukas Hoyer, Yannick Strümpler et al. · Google, Ulm University

items.title: Benchmarks Are Surprisingly Compaction-Friendly
items.tldr: When long-running coding agents summarize their context to keep going, benchmark scores barely change, but the rules they were given quietly disappear from the summaries.
items.byline: Jeanne Salle, Hardik Bhatnagar, Matthias Bethge et al. · ELLIS Institute Tübingen, Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems, Tübingen AI Center

items.title: Nested Sparsity for Scalable Pretraining and Continual Learning
items.tldr: Nestor routes each token to a few attention "columns" that each contain their own experts, extending mixture-of-experts sparsity to attention and making it 13-29% more compute-efficient than MoE transformers.
items.byline: Tianzhe Chu, Druv Pai, Yi Ma · University of Hong Kong, UC Berkeley

items.title: DiscoDemo: Discovering Efficient and Diverse Robot Demonstrations for Imitation Learning
items.tldr: Training a simulated RL "demonstrator" to find many different successful solutions, rather than one, doubles the real-robot success of a vision-language-action policy trained on its demos.
items.byline: Minho Park, Kinam Kim, Donghu Kim et al. · KAIST, Holiday Robotics
